Exercise A

Two Weeks at the Animal Clinic

Read the text about Lena's work experience. Choose the correct word for each gap.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Reading Text

Every year, students in Year 9 spend two weeks doing work experience. They leave the classroom and work in a real 1. Their teachers hope that they will find out what a normal working 2 really looks like.

Lena has just finished her two weeks at a small animal 3 near her home. On the first morning she was very 4, because she had never worked with a vet before.

Her first 5 were simple. She cleaned the waiting room, brought water to the animals and answered the telephone. After a few days the vet let her 6 a small operation.

“I have learnt a lot about myself,” Lena says. “I have never been so tired in my life, but I have also never been so 7.”

Her teacher says that work experience helps young people to choose a 8. Some students discover a job they love. Others find out which job is definitely not right for them — and that is useful too.

Exercise B

Present Perfect or Simple Past?

Use the simple past when you say when something happened (yesterday, last week, in May). Use the present perfect when the time is not important, or when something started in the past and is still true (since, for, so far, never, already).

Complete the Sentence

1. Lena her placement last Friday.

2. She three applications so far this year.

3. My brother in a garage since 2023.

4. We our work experience in May.

5. I have never in an office.

6. you ever visited a factory?

7. When you start your placement?

8. Anna already finished her report.

Exercise D

Writing: My Work Experience

Write 6–8 sentences about work experience. Use at least two present perfect sentences and two simple past sentences.

Think about these questions

• Which job would you like to try — and why?

• Have you ever worked, helped in a shop, or looked after children or animals?

• What did you do, and what did you learn?

• Which job would definitely not be right for you?

You can use these: I have never... I have already... Last summer I... so far for two weeks I would like to work as... because I learnt that...
Your text
Aim for 6–8 sentences with two present perfect and two simple past forms.
